key_insight: ONCOTIMIA integrates a secure, modular GenAI pipeline to automatically populate lung cancer tumour board forms, reducing the manual documentation burden for multidisciplinary tumour boards (MDTBs).
problem_solved: Addresses the time-consuming, error-prone process of structuring heterogeneous clinical data for MDTBs by automating extraction and form completion while maintaining clinical workflow integration and data security.
method: Modular, secure pipeline that connects clinical data sources to a tuned large language model for clinical text understanding and generation.
Structured information extraction (NLP) + LLM-driven template filling to auto-complete tumour board forms for lung cancer cases.
Clinician-in-the-loop evaluation within MDTB workflows to validate outputs and ensure safety, relevance and interoperability with existing systems.
impact: Demonstrates a practical path for responsibly deploying LLMs in clinical workflows, reducing documentation workload and improving MDTB efficiency while highlighting the need for clinician oversight and secure integrations. This informs AI/ML practitioners about design patterns for clinical GenAI applications.
visual_elements: End-to-end pipeline diagram: data sources → secure preprocessing → LLM module → filled tumour board form → clinician review
Before vs. after infographic (manual vs. automated) showing reduced steps/time and lower documentation load
System architecture chart emphasizing modular components and data governance (encryption, audit, access control)
Annotated example tumour board form showing input text, extracted entities, and LLM-generated fields
paper_title: Evaluation of Oncotimia: An LLM based system for supporting tumour boards
paper_authors: Luis Lorenzo, Marcos Montana-Mendez, Sergio Figueiras, Miguel Boubeta, Cristobal Bernardo-Castineira
